chunks.text:
Look, you pick one door out of three, meaning you almost certainly picked a goat. The host knows where the car is, and his job is to reveal a goat from the doors you didn't pick. He isn't guessing; he’s actively filtering out a wrong answer for you. That means whenever your first pick was wrong—which happens most of the time—switching guarantees you win the car. 

If there were a million doors and you picked one, then the host opened 999,998 goats and left just one other door standing, you’d switch in a heartbeat.

***

**The most common misunderstanding:** 
People assume that because only two doors remain, it must be an even 50/50 coin flip, completely overlooking that the host's insider knowledge biased which door was left behind.
